data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small, independently operated services is more resilient to correlated failure than a large service with strictly more total redundancy, provided the network's 'diversity coefficient' exceeds the monolith's 'homogeneity threshold'.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized network converges on a 'virtual monolith' by adopting identical industry-standard substrates (e.g., all using the same cloud region or container orchestrator).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The monolith implements N-version programming, where redundancy is achieved through functionally equivalent but independently developed implementations.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The monolith's redundancy is typically linear (identical replicas), creating a single failure domain where a specific bug or configuration error propagates instantly across all redundant nodes. In contrast, a decentralized network utilizes combinatorial diversity; because operators use different OS kernels, hardware, and configuration patterns (intentional or accidental), a failure mode targeting a specific implementation only affects a subset of the network, preventing systemic collapse.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
